alt.en: A parchment scroll lying open in a museum case: one column of handwritten Hebrew in black ink between two rolled-up ends. The left roller is capped with silver filigree set with red and green beads; the right end is rolled loose.
alt.es: Un rollo de pergamino abierto en una vitrina de museo: una columna de hebreo escrito a mano con tinta negra entre los dos extremos enrollados. El rodillo de la izquierda lleva un remate de filigrana de plata con cuentas rojas y verdes; el extremo de la derecha está enrollado suelto.

caption.en: A handwritten Hebrew scroll of Esther from the 18th century, open at the verse that brings in Mordecai (Esther 2:5), one of the four verses the congregation sings aloud during the reading.
caption.es: Un rollo de Ester escrito a mano en hebreo, del siglo XVIII, abierto en el versículo que presenta a Mardoqueo (Ester 2:5), uno de los cuatro versículos que la congregación canta en voz alta durante la lectura.

source: Book of Esther, Hebrew, c. 1700-1800 AD, on display in the Wirth Gallery of the Middle East, Royal Ontario Museum; photograph DSC09614 by Daderot, 20 November 2011
library: Royal Ontario Museum, Toronto (photograph via Wikimedia Commons)
callNumber: Wikimedia Commons, File:Book of Esther, Hebrew, c. 1700-1800 AD - Royal Ontario Museum - DSC09614.JPG
licenceEvidence: Commons file page, first revision 64498358 (2011-12-28) by the photographer Daderot: "I took this photograph and release it into the public domain", Permission {{cc0}}; the API gives LicenseShortName "CC0". The scroll itself is 18th century, its scribe unknown, so public domain by age (see rights.md).
credit: Photograph by Daderot (CC0), Royal Ontario Museum, Toronto

alt.en: An architect's drawing in ink and pale green wash on cream paper. Above, the long side of a synagogue: tall round-arched windows between a domed tower at each end. Below, the floor plan: rows of benches on either side of a central aisle and a raised platform at the far end. A handwritten Swedish title runs across the top.
alt.es: Un dibujo de arquitecto en tinta y aguada verde pálido sobre papel crema. Arriba, el costado largo de una sinagoga: altas ventanas de arco de medio punto entre dos torres con cúpula, una en cada extremo. Abajo, la planta: filas de bancos a ambos lados de un pasillo central y una plataforma elevada al fondo. Un título manuscrito en sueco cruza la parte de arriba.

caption.en: August Krüger's approved drawing of 1852 for the synagogue of Gothenburg's Jewish congregation, its long side and floor plan; Abraham Baer was cantor of the new synagogue, consecrated in 1855, from 1857 to 1894.
caption.es: El dibujo aprobado de August Krüger, de 1852, para la sinagoga de la comunidad judía de Gotemburgo, con su costado largo y su planta; Abraham Baer fue cantor de la nueva sinagoga, consagrada en 1855, de 1857 a 1894.

source: Göteborg, Synagogan. Ritningar till fasader och plan, Göteborgs stift, Göteborgs och Bohus län. Aug. Krüger 1852-05-04: "Ritning till Långfacade af Synagogbyggnaden å Mosaiska Församlingens Tomter", sheet 2
library: Riksarkivet (National Archives of Sweden), Överintendentsämbetet drawings
callNumber: Riksarkivet record t8odREDPgaYVbrWhIzxUa2; sheet stamped "Synagogan i Göteborg. G 175"
licenceEvidence: Drawn and approved 1852 ("I nåder gillad d. 4 maj 1852" on the sheet); architect August Krüger died 1896 (Wikidata Q20257365), the countersigning Ludvig Hedin by 1917. Commons file page (Riksarkivet cooperation project): {{PD-old}}, source National Archives of Sweden. A faithful scan of a flat work adds no new copyright (see rights.md).

alt.en: Six lines of Hebrew type with vowel points on cream paper, beginning with an indented line, and ending with a short last line followed by a colon-like stop.
alt.es: Seis líneas de texto hebreo impreso con vocales sobre papel crema; la primera línea va sangrada y la última, más corta, termina con un signo de puntuación parecido a dos puntos.

caption.en: Shoshanat Yaakov and the lines after it, ending with Harbona remembered for good, in the Hebrew of Simeon Singer's Standard Prayer Book (New York, 1915), page 423.
caption.es: Shoshanat Yaakov y los versos que la siguen, hasta el de Harbona recordado para bien, en el hebreo del Standard Prayer Book de Simeon Singer (Nueva York, 1915), página 423.

source: Simeon Singer, trans., The Standard Prayer Book (New York: Bloch Publishing, 1915), "Service for Purim", Hebrew p. 423
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive standardprayerbo00hagg, leaf n850; call number 461990
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1915 (IA metadata "possible-copyright-status": "NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT"); translator Simeon Singer died 1906; the Hebrew liturgy is centuries old and anonymous. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A strip of printed music: three lines on single treble staves in two flats, headed "No. 197. Solo. Andantino." and the Hebrew title Shoshanat Yaakov, with the words in German-style transliteration under the notes. A short last line after a double bar is marked "Leise weiter."
alt.es: Una franja de música impresa: tres líneas en pentagramas simples de clave de sol con dos bemoles, encabezadas "No. 197. Solo. Andantino." y con el título hebreo Shoshanat Yaakov, y la letra transliterada a la alemana bajo las notas. Una última línea corta, tras una doble barra, lleva la indicación "Leise weiter."

caption.en: Shoshanat Yaakov as No. 197 on page 59 of Abraham Baer's Baal T'fillah (third edition, Frankfurt am Main, after 1883), the soft last line marked "Leise weiter": the page our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: Shoshanat Yaakov como n.º 197 en la página 59 del Baal T'fillah de Abraham Baer (tercera edición, Frankfurt am Main, después de 1883), con el suave verso final marcado "Leise weiter": la página de la que está tomado nuestro arreglo.

source: Abraham Baer, Baal T'fillah oder Der practische Vorbeter, 3rd edition (Frankfurt am Main: J. Kauffmann, after 1883), p. 59, No. 197
library: Internet Archive (a 2024 upload that names no holding library)
licenceEvidence: Printed after 1883 (first edition 1877); Abraham Baer died 1894, so life plus 70 ended 1964; the tune is anonymous. IA item marked Public Domain Mark 1.0 by its uploader. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
